articles.content: If you wanted to be a completionist for the movies of documentary legend Frederick Wiseman , or if you have a blind spot for Wiseman’s formalist portraits of American institutions dating back decades, today is your lucky day. Janus Films has acquired the North American distribution rights to the complete collection of 45 feature films from Wiseman’s career dating back to his seminal “Titicut Follies” in 1967, and Janus plans to distribute all of them beginning January 1, 2027. Janus already has a library that includes the works of Agnès Varda, Ingmar Bergman, Akira Kurosawa, Chantal Akerman, and Edward Yang, so Wiseman finds himself in good company. But Wiseman’s early films, everything from “Titicut Follies” in 1967 through “State Legislature” in 2007 have been restored in 4K by Wiseman’s Zipporah Films. “La Danse” (2009) through his final feature “ Menus-Plaisirs – Les Troisgros ” (2023) will be available in their original digital formats. This is the first time any distributor other than Zipporah Films is licensing Wiseman’s work in North America, so the hope is that the late documentarian can now reach an even greater audience. articles.content: In 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves. The 1948 Paramount Decrees (named after the studio that pioneered the vertical integration) required studios to give up one of the three options. They decided to give up exhibition. The choice was easy: With low margins on ticket sales and the need to constantly bring audiences in, who wanted to run a movie theater ? 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition. The rise of streaming was said to bring about the end of theaters as we know them. But the COVID-19 pandemic brought exhibition to its closest brink of extinction yet. After the global pandemic, lockdown protocols forced movie theaters to close for months. The luxury theater chain Arclight shuttered all its locations within weeks. Locations closed at a variety of companies, including Alamo Drafthouse. Some theaters survived off of private rentals. Even as theaters slowly reopened, COVID protocols required leaving some seats empty, meaning not all tickets could be sold. “I think there was no right move,” League added. “We laid most of our people off. We spent a lot of energy trying to build up a TVOD streaming platform which didn’t entirely work for a lot of reasons… And so we went through bankruptcy, and it was rough. articles.content: Netflix is the proud new owner of Radford Studio Center , the 98-year-old soundstage complex that was home to “Gunsmoke,” “The Mary Tyler Moore Show,” and “Seinfeld.” The streamer is set to close the $380 million acquisition this afternoon, the company said in a statement. The facility last sold to Hackman Capital Partners for $1.85 billion at the peak of the L.A. production market in 2021. The subsequent downturn in production volume and the rise in interest rates forced Hackman to default on its $1.1 billion loan, and ultimately to cede the property to its lender, Goldman Sachs. Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Returns to Imax 70mm Theaters Again After Record-Breaking Run Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done Netflix first emerged as a buyer of the 55-acre site in Studio City last spring. Goldman formally took the property back at a foreclosure auction on Tuesday, the final step before the deal with Netflix could close. The purchase marks a significant investment in Los Angeles for Netflix, which has made similar investments in Albuquerque, N.M., and Fort Monmouth, N.J., in recent years. “There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California’s film industry,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday. “This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.” Hackman Capital Partners proposed a $1 billion renovation of the aging Radford lot in 2023. Netflix is expected to continue that ongoing entitlement process with the city as it looks to preserve its development options and its ability to respond to market conditions. articles.content: Philip Rosenberg , the production designer who won an Oscar for his work on All That Jazz and also worked on films such as Network , Moonstruck and The Hurricane , has died , according to his nephew, Alan Rosenberg. No cause of death was given. He was 91. Rosenberg was raised in Brooklyn before studying scenic design at Yale University with Donald Oenslager. About that time, he was hired as an assistant at the Metropolitan Opera where he worked with Ita Maximovna and Eugene Berman. His first film was The Seagull in 1968, on which he was a design assistant. Among Rosenberg’s first starry projects was Herbert Ross’ The Owl and the Pussycat in 1970. Rosenberg was the art director on the film starring Barbra Streisand and George Segal. He transitioned to production designer on James Toback’s The Gambler before making a splash in 1976’s new Hollywood landmark Network , becoming known for the realism which made that period’s films stand out. Watch on Deadline After Network , Rosenberg would go on to work with direction Sidney Lumet on Daniel, Garbo Talks, Running on Empty and many more. He likewise had a long-running working relationship with Norman Jewison. The two collaborated on Moonstruck , Other People’s Money , The January Man (which Jewison produced) and The Hurricane . Rosenberg’s breakthrough came on All That Jazz in 1978. His work on Bob Fosse’s film earned him an Oscar, which he shared with Tony Walton, Edward Stewart and Gary J. Brink. articles.content: Philip Rosenberg, a production designer and art director who was part of the team that won the art direction-set decoration Oscar for “ All That Jazz ,” died Oct. 28 in West Palm Beach, Florida. He was 91. Rosenberg’s first film job was as design assistant on the 1968 “The Sea Gull.” He went on to become an art director and production designer, working with New York-based directors such as Sidney Lumet, Paul Mazursky and Norman Jewison. Known for being part of the realist school of production design in the 1970s, he was nominated for an Oscar as art director of “The Wiz.” Among his other credits were “The Owl and the Pussycat,” “Next Stop Greenwich Village,” “The Gambler,” “Network,” “The Sentinel,” “Running on Empty,” “Night Falls on Manhattan” and “Moonstruck.” His final credit came for “Collateral Damage” in 2002. articles.content: As the nation remains enthralled by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes film “You Can See Everything,” the first documentary to cross $100 million at the global box office in over two decades, arguably the most influential — and the most prolific — documentarian in American cinema’s works have found a new home. Related Stories Maya Jama Strikes Deal With Netflix (EXCLUSIVE) 'Dune: Prophecy' Star Tabu Joins YRF Entertainment's Netflix Rescue Drama 'Tunnel Men' (EXCLUSIVE) Asked about the casting in an interview with U.K. retiree magazine Saga , Osman said: “You probably won’t believe this, but it had nothing to do with me. Before moving in front of the camera he was creative director at “Deal or No Deal” producer Endemol U.K., which was eventually acquired by Banijay. Variety ‘s reviewer called “The Thursday Murder Club” adaptation “as amiable and inoffensive as they come,” concluding: “As a riff on the British whodunit, Columbus’ film is simply a cozy, and perhaps an all too simple, affair.”

articles.summary: The comedy is "a crisply paced romp featuring pitch-perfect performances by adversarial leads Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller."
articles.content: On Oct. 6, 2000, moviegoers met Greg Focker and Co. for the first time as Meet the Parents hit theaters. The Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller comedy scored $330 million and launched a franchise that now totals four movies . The Hollywood Reporter’s original review is below: Proving that there’s life after Austin Powers , director Jay Roach finds his comic mojo winningly intact with Meet the Parents . The three words that instill instant dread in any prospective suitor are taken to their logical, side-splitting extreme in a crisply paced romp featuring pitch-perfect performances by adversarial leads Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller. With its built-in ability to strike a multigenerational, universal chord, this Universal and DreamWorks joint effort should handily emerge as one of the season’s top comedies. articles.title: Antoine Fuqua Accused of Pointing Handgun, Using Antisemitic Slur in Assault Lawsuit
articles.summary: A spokesperson for the director denied the allegations and said, "It's not true."
articles.content: Director Antoine Fuqua has been sued for assault and battery by a bar manager, who alleges the director struck him with a handgun and used an antisemitic slur. In a lawsuit filed on Friday in California state court, the bar manager, William Rosenthal, details an altercation in February in which Fuqua and his group were denied entry to a Los Angeles bar because they were overly intoxicated. He claims the director “directed a racial and antisemitic slur” at him before the filmmaker and his son “pointed their handguns” in his direction. Related Stories Business Selena Gomez's Wondermind Fraud Lawsuit Has Been Dismissed With Prejudice TV Chris Pratt Seeks Violent Redemption in 'The Terminal List' Season 2 First-Look Images Rosenthal brings claims for assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress. He seeks at least $50,000. In a statement, a spokesperson for the director denied the allegations. “It’s not true,” the representative said. The lawsuit says Fuqua and four others, including his daughter and son, visited Good Times at Davey Wayne’s in Los Angeles on Feb. 14. After the group was refused entry by Rosenthal, he was spat on by a member of the group and threatened by Fuqua’s daughter, according to the complaint. They left the establishment, the lawsuit says. Roughly an hour later, Fuqua returned and confronted Rosenthal about pepper spraying his daughter. Rosenthal denied the accusation and was hit in the face with a handgun by the director, who later used an antisemitic slur and threatened to kill the bar manager. From there, the altercation escalated, with Fuqua’s son also pulling out a handgun and striking Rosenthal, the lawsuit says. Rosenthal says he sustained a head injury, nose fracture and lacerations from the alleged assault and now has post-traumatic stress disorder and severe emotional stress. His lawyers say the injuries will result in “some permanent disability.”

articles.title: Sadie Sandler to Star in Netflix Horror Movie ‘Malibu’ From Vertigo, Happy Madison (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Room 101 also produces director Tod "Kip" Williams' feature about a dog-sitting gig gone wrong.
articles.content: Sadie Sandler is set to make a splash as she prepares to star in her first horror movie. The actress, who recently led the Netflix comedy Roommates , will collaborate again with the streamer on the horror feature Malibu , The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Tod “Kip” Williams, known for helming Paranormal Activity 2 , is set to direct the film from a script he wrote with Tom Pabst, who worked on the superhero series Titans . Production will begin in early 2027 for the feature that counts Roy Lee ‘s Vertigo Entertainment , Steven Schneider’s Room 101 and Adam Sandler ‘s Happy Madison as producers. Malibu centers on Sadie Sandler as an aspiring actress who accepts a last-minute dog-sitting job at a reclusive movie star’s Malibu mansion. Soon, she learns that the house is not what she expected. While Sandler appeared in Netflix’s 2020 spooky comedy Hubie Halloween opposite dad Adam Sandler and has voiced a role in Sony Pictures’ animated Hotel Transylvania franchise, Malibu is described as straight horror and is said to carry a much different tone from her previous projects. Sadie Sandler recently appeared on Netflix’s Nobody Wants This , and her feature credits include Roommates , Jay Kelly , Happy Gilmore 2 and You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah . In addition to helming Paranormal Activity 2 , Williams directed John Cusack and Samuel L. Jackson in the 2016 movie Cell that adapted Stephen King’s sci-fi horror novel. Lee, who was named THR’ s producer of the year in 2025, has served as executive producer on such horror series as Peacock’s Crystal Lake and HBO’s It: Welcome to Derry . His recent feature credits include Resident Evil , Weapons , A Minecraft Movie and Obsession director Curry Barker’s forthcoming movie Anything but Ghosts .

articles.summary: Focus Features is developing the feature that is based on author Kevin Barry's 2024 Western novel.
articles.content: Spielberg is developing an untitled feature adaptation of author Kevin Barry’s 2024 novel The Heart in Winter for Focus Features . Anderson is writing the screenplay for the project that he will produce with Spielberg, Kristie Macosko Krieger and Sara Murphy, with Spielberg attached to direct. Jessie Buckley , Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance are the trio of Oscar winners set to star in the movie that is eyeing a 2028 theatrical release. Barry’s novel is set in 1891 in Montana and follows Tom Rourke and Polly Gillespie, who elope and steal a horse. The pair end up being pursued by a number of violent men who seek their capture. Tim Headington, Neil Shah, Ryan Zacarias and Ana Leocha are set to executive produce. Earlier this year, Spielberg helmed Universal’s Disclosure Day . He also produced Focus’ Hamnet , which hit theaters late last year from director Chloé Zhao and earned an Oscar for Buckley. Anderson is coming off the success of Warner Bros.’ 2025 release One Battle After Another , which collected six Oscars, including Anderson’s wins for best picture, director and adapted screenplay. During an interview last year with Dazed , the filmmaker confirmed that he did uncredited script work on Martin Scorsese’s Killers of the Flower Moon and Ridley Scott’s Napoleon. Spielberg told The Hollywood Reporter last year that he still hoped to someday direct a Western. He explained that he has an “appetite for a Western, which I will someday hopefully do. It’s something that’s eluded me for all of these decades.” Buckley is represented by CAA, United Agents, and Johnson Shapiro. Murphy is repped by WME and Sloane Offer. articles.title: TV Ratings: NBA Logs Winning Streak in First Month of the Season
articles.summary: Audiences on national media partners NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are up by 37 percent year to year.
articles.content: Like a jump shooter who can’t miss, the NBA is on a heater with TV audiences through the first month of its 2026-27 season. National telecasts of league games on NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are averaging 2.62 million viewers over the season’s first month, based on Nielsen ratings and Adobe Analytics figures for Peacock’s games. That’s a sizable, 37 percent increase over the same time frame last year — the first in the league’s current media rights deal with NBCUniversal, ESPN and Prime Video. Through last week, every national telecast had topped 1 million viewers, the first time that’s happened since 2023. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: CMA Awards Score Seven-Year High TV Streaming Ratings: Rough Week for Original Series, 'From' Remains No. 1 Overall That’s also the highest mark on record for the first month of an NBA season, excluding lockout-delayed starts in 1999 and 2011 (and with the caveat that changes in Nielsen measurement the past few years have tended to benefit live sports). NBC’s six national windows lead the way with an average of 4.5 million viewers (including streaming on Peacock), a 27 percent improvement over last season’s first month.. The network’s opening night game between the defending champion New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers (who acquired LeBron James during the offseason) averaged 7.71 million cross-platform viewers. The first eight games on Prime Video have averaged 2.05 million viewers, and ESPN is at 1.8 million viewers across 13 telecasts. Prime Video has grown by a huge 83 percent year to year, and ESPN’s games are up 13 percent. Prime Video has the youngest audience of the NBA’s three national media partners (the same is true for Prime relative to other NFL broadcasters); its median viewer age is a little under 46. ESPN and NBC (not including Peacock viewers) have a median age of about 53 for NBA games.

articles.content: Steven Hack, the theater veteran who spent five years on Broadway as an original castmember in Cats , then appeared as a character actor in dozens of films and TV shows, has died. He was 68. Hack died Thursday at home following what was described as “a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the Interact Theatre Company announced . He was a founding member of the North Hollywood-based group that launched in 1989. “Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist and a cherished member of our artistic family,” ITC directors Barry Heins and Walter Ware said in a statement. “His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years, and his artistry, humor, warmth and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.” Related Stories Lifestyle The Pulitzer-Winning Play 'Purpose' Finally Came to Los Angeles. But That Doesn't Mean It's Gone Hollywood. Hack was there when Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on Oct. 7, 1982, and he portrayed several characters, including Coricopat, Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Tumblebrutus and Pouncival, over the next five years. He toured with Michael Bennett’s A Chorus Line for nearly two years and then joined the Broadway production at the Shubert Theatre for one show only — its record-breaking 3,389th Great White Way performance on Sept. 29, 1983. (He did Cats that night, too.) Hack started showing up on television in the 1990s on shows including The Trials of Rosie O’Neill , Jake and the Fatman , Matlock , Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman , Married … With Children , Seinfeld , Mad About You and Caroline in the City . The Social Network and Fight Club filmmaker says he was approached to creatively lead big-budget The Lord of the Rings prequel series — and turned it down. “I got offered — what is the Lord of the Rings thing at Amazon?” Fincher asked Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast . “Oh, Rings of Power ,” the host said. articles.title: ‘Glee’ Star Says Cory Monteith Tribute Should Not Have Been Filmed So Soon After His Death
articles.summary: "We were grieving both privately and publicly," notes Jenna Ushkowitz of her late co-star, who died of a drug overdose in 2013 The post ‘Glee’ Star Says Cory Monteith Tribute Should Not Have Been Filmed So Soon After His Death appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: “We were grieving both privately and publicly,” notes Jenna Ushkowitz of her late co-star, who died of a drug overdose in 2013 “Glee” star Jenna Ushkowitz says the show’s Season 5 tribute to Corey Monteith should not have been filmed so soon after his death. “It was like too soon for that,” Ushkowitz told the “We Need to Talk” podcast about the period following Monteith’s death. The actor died from a drug overdose on July 13, 2013 at age 31. “Was not fun. Don’t want to remember that time,” she added. Production on the tribute episode, titled “The Quarterback” after Monteith’s character Finn, reportedly began on August 23, 2013, five weeks after Monteith’s death. “Nobody had the tools,” Ushkowitz recalled of how the cast and crew felt at the time. “To shoot ‘The Quarterback’ was just, I think it wasn’t the right thing. And I think everybody collectively agrees that that’s maybe not the thing we should have done, because we were grieving both privately and publicly.” “I think the fans definitely needed something because they loved Cory so dearly like we did. And Finn so dearly. But it’s a really hard thing to be grieving your friend and being a character grieving their friend at the same time,” she added. “We’ve mourned Cory, but now we’re mourning Finn. So it’s kind of like two people in that one person,” Matthew Morrison told E! News at the time. Morrison played Will Schuester for all six seasons of the FOX musical show, which wrapped in 2015. Tragedy would strike the “Glee” cast twice more, with Mark Salling (Puck) dying by suicide in 2018 and Naya Rivera (Santana) drowning in 2020 . In October 2016, a “Glee” reboot was greenlit , with Disney+ and Hulu granting a series order from 20th Television, 17 years after the original series first launched on Fox.

articles.title: ‘DWTS’ Finale: What Jan Ravnik Said That Got Bleeped Out
articles.summary: The professional dancer let an expletive slip following his partner Tatyana Ali's freestyle routine The post ‘DWTS’ Finale: What Jan Ravnik Said That Got Bleeped Out appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The professional dancer let an expletive slip following his partner Tatyana Ali’s freestyle routine Jan Ravnik dropped an expletive after he and his partner Tatyana Ali performed their freestyle routine on the “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 finale Tuesday night. Co-host Julianne Hough noticed the professional dancer becoming emotional after his first freestyle dance and asked what he was feeling. He held back his tears but let something else slip. “She f–king killed it,” Ravnik said after sarcastically revealing that Hough was on his “Dead to Me” list. The expletive was bleeped out on the live broadcast on ABC and Disney+, but the audience in the ballroom heard it loud and clear. The duo were one of five finalists in the “DWTS” finale. They performed a futuristic freestyle routine to “Minnie the Moocher” by Cab Calloway and “Over the Rainbow” by Judy Garland. Ali and Ravnik kicked off the night with a salsa routine to “Jamaican (Bam Bam)” by HUGEL & SOLTO (FR), where she earned all 9s. Her instant dance round was a jive, which caught the actress off guard before she blew the judges away. The other competitors going for the Mirrorball Trophy included Maura Higgins, Connor Wood, Amber Glenn and Ezra Frech. For the first time in the show’s history, “Dancing With the Stars” aired live nationwide for its finale. While the ballroom competition show typically airs three hours later on the West Coast than its East Coast airing, the three-hour finale aired live in every U.S. time zone. The change-up in airing times meant that viewers would be able to vote live for their favorite couples as the finale unfolded and the finale five couples were narrowed down to one winning couple. During the finale, reigning champion Robert Irwin announced that “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” was renewed for a second season and that fans could apply. “Dancing with the Stars” is produced in front of a live audience by BBC Studios Los Angeles Productions.

articles.title: Cult Classic ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters With Poster Parodying ‘The Devils’

articles.content: Mike Cheslik’s slapstick film is coming back to 85 cities for its third annual Christmas re-release A few years ago, an utterly insane slapstick masterpiece called “Hundreds of Beavers” snuck upon an unsuspecting indie film world, creating a new cult classic that has remained in at least one theater in America every day since. Now, as part of what director Mike Cheslik and producer Kurt Ravenwood hopes will become an annual tradition, “Hundreds of Beavers” will be re-released in select theaters in 85 cities. And to get fans excited, the team has released beaver-themed posters parodying three of the most talked about films of the fall among cinephiles: “You Can See Everything,” “Digger,” and Ken Russell’s “The Devils,” the NC-17 drama released uncut by Warner Bros. for the first time ever this past October. “Hundreds of Beavers” stars Ryland Tews as Jean Kayak, a man brought to ruin when beavers — played by dozens of actors in beaver suits — destroy his successful applejack brewery. Left with nothing, Jean must learn to survive as a hunter and fur trapper in the cold northern wilderness … and in the process gets into a ridiculous conflict with hundreds of beavers. In addition to the film, the re-release will have a new short made by Cheslik as part of the annual tradition. Previous shorts have introduced characters like “Bing Crosbeaver” and “Conspirabeaver,” and now they will be joined by a sinister new foe. Released in 2024 with a marketing budget of just $70,000, “Hundreds of Beavers” sold out arthouses across the country with a roadshow that caught the attention of the growing Letterboxd crowd. The film was then re-released theatrically at Christmas to promote its release on Blu-Ray, which Cheslik is now turning into an annual tradition. articles.title: Phillip Picardi Exits Playboy After 8 Months as Chief Brand Officer and Editor-in-Chief
articles.summary: The veteran editor, who also co-founded Them, was appointed to both roles in March 2026 The post Phillip Picardi Exits Playboy After 8 Months as Chief Brand Officer and Editor-in-Chief appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The veteran editor, who also co-founded Them, was appointed to both roles in March 2026 Phillip Picardi is exiting Playboy as it’s chief content officer and editor in chief after just eight months, TheWrap has confirmed. Picardi was appointed to both roles in March 2026. His exit date has not been announced, but a rep for Playboy confirmed he will be departing. “Thrilled to be officially joining Playboy in this capacity, and I can’t wait to show more of you what we’ve been cooking,” Picardi posted on Instagram back in March. Prior to joining Playboy, Picardi served as chief brand officer at WeightWatchers and chief strategy officer at the Los Angeles LGBT Center. His previous editorial roles included editor in chief of Out magazine, chief content officer at Teen Vogue and chief content officer and founder of Condé Nast’s queer-focused publication Them. Under his leadership at Playboy, which relaunched its print magazine as a quarterly publication in 2025, three issues were released featuring Karol G, Cara DeLevingne and Charli XCX as cover models. Others features launched included “Playboy’s Guide to Drugs” (both in print and online) and the hidden history behind Marilyn Monroe’s lost cover (Monroe was the men’s magazine’s very first centerfold). In August, Picardi introduced the new Playboy global headquarters in Miami Beach, Fla. In the Instagram post , Picardi revealed that “none of my belongings have arrived from L.A. yet.” Puck was the first to report Picardi’s depature and said he would remain with the company for a few months to launch the next issue before returning to Los Angeles.

articles.title: Broadway Stagehands Avoid Strike After Reaching Tentative Agreement With Theater Operators
articles.summary: Meanwhile, theatrical wardrobe workers remain without a contract The post Broadway Stagehands Avoid Strike After Reaching Tentative Agreement With Theater Operators appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: IATSE Local One, the union that represents Broadway stagehands, reached a tentative agreement with The Broadway League on Tuesday, avoiding a strike that likely would have shut down productions during the busy holiday season. The previous agreement between IATSE Local One and The Broadway League, which represents theater owners and producers, expired July 26. According to the IATSE website , Local One sought wage and benefit increases for its members. The new agreement still needs to be ratified at the next Local One membership meeting in December. However, the contract fight continues for Theatrical Wardrobe Union, IATSE Local 764. Wardrobe workers unanimously voted Sunday to authorize a strike as they continue working without a contract. However, no strike has been called at this time. “Among the major unresolved issues are wages and a longstanding gender pay gap affecting Broadway wardrobe workers,” IATSE said in a press release Tuesday. “Wardrobe work on Broadway has historically been performed predominantly by women and paid at significantly lower rates than stagehand classifications historically held predominantly by men. Although recent negotiations have narrowed that gap, Local 764 department heads today must work nearly 45 percent longer to earn pay comparable to workers in similar department-head roles.” The holidays are traditionally Broadway’s busiest season, as tourists flock to New York City for Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s. IATSE, the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees, represents 170,000 technicians, artisans and craftspeople in the entertainment industry in the United States and Canada.

articles.title: Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56
articles.summary: In addition to being a 25-year veteran of the festival, Plante was a director in his own right.
articles.content: Mike Plante , a filmmaker and 25-year veteran of the Sundance Institute, died Tuesday after a brief illness. He was 56. At Sundance, Plante worked as a Shorts Programmer and was a familiar, warm-hearted presence at festival screenings and events . “Mike was a treasure to the Institute, the Festival, and our independent film community,” Sundance Festival Director Eugene Hernandez and Director of Programming Kim Yutani said in a joint statement. “His sense of wonder and humor were matched by boundless enthusiasm and curatorial excellence. Our Festival’s Short Film Program and the Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour were shaped by Mike’s energy and superb taste in movies. Mike’s roots at Sundance Institute, and his relationships within our organization and festival, run deep. He will be remembered and deeply missed as a true cinephile, a filmmaker, a champion of short films, movie theaters, and film culture.” Related Stories Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? articles.summary: Milton S. Hershey gets the Angel Studios treatment in a deranged and decidedly vanilla piece of "values-based entertainment."

The bigger they got (on the strength of projects like “The Chosen” and the QAnon cause célèbre “Sound of Freedom,” the latter of which pioneered a questionable ticketing model that continues today), the more that Angel removed from the films they released. Not just sex and swear words, but also anything that even vaguely resembled a soul. articles.content: Awards season will be making a stop in San Francisco on December 7 for the annual SFFILM Awards Night , honoring four artists who’ve made an impact this year. John Turturro , acclaimed this year for his performance in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” will receive the Maria Manetti Shrem Award for Acting, named for the Italian-American philanthropist. (Turturro will also receive IndieWire Honors recognition on December 3.) Carrie Coon , who made a big-screen splash this year in “The Liberation,” will receive the Katie & Todd Traina Award for Acting. The SFFILM Award for Virtuosity will go to “La Bola Negra” breakout star and beloved Spanish pop singer Guitarricadelafuente. Finally, the Nion McEvoy & Leslie Berriman Award for Storytelling goes to “ I Play Rocky ” screenwriter Peter Gamble. articles.title: Watch the ‘Project Hail Mary’ VFX Supervisor Explain Why Having Puppeteers on Set Was Worth All the Extra Work
articles.summary: Mag Sarnowska and her team had to remove a lot of reflections from the sci-fi epic, but she wouldn't have it any other way.
articles.content: The making of “Project Hail Mary” was a miracle on par with the outer space rescue mission that Ryan Gosling is tasked with pulling off. Phil Lord and Chris Miller’s adaptation of Andy Weir’s bestselling novel manages to be epic without ever losing its intimacy, as Gosling traverses the galaxy and saves the world with only a very lovable rock acting alongside him. The final product was a complicated blend of practical effects, on-set puppetry, and a healthy dose of VFX magic. Incorporating so many production elements creates more work for all involved. The puppetry team lead by James Ortiz had to fit into very small spaces, which frequently meant they showed up in the frames. Visual Effects Production Supervisor Mag Sarnowska and her team were tasked with removing all of the puppeteers. But as she explained during the VFX panel at IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables, it was a small price to pay for the way it enhanced Gosling’s acting performance. articles.title: The Extraordinary Music Worthy of an Extraordinary Life in ‘W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel with a Cause’
articles.summary: Composer Kathryn Bostic and director Rita Coburn tell IndieWire how they drew from Du Bois' own encounters with a broad array of musical influences to shape their film's score.
articles.content: Rita Coburn ‘s “ W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel with a Cause ” is an extraordinary documentary about an extraordinary man, a film that spans nearly 100 years in two hours, yet never feels rushed or superficial. In her storytelling, Coburn shares with her subject a talent for distilling complex ideas and expressing them with force and clarity; the result is a movie that fully honors the breadth and depth of Du Bois’ achievements as a groundbreaking Black writer, historian, and activist. One of Coburn’s most potent tools in this regard is the music by composer Kathryn Bostic , who previously collaborated with the director on “Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands.” Bostic incorporates a wide array of styles and influences in her score, which references the various types of music Du Bois encountered and appreciated as a Black intellectual but isn’t beholden to them; as evocative of Bach and American folk music as it is of 19th-century spirituals and Asian motifs, it’s the sonic equivalent of Du Bois’ literary works.
